sourceEvidence.title: PMAY-U official guideline index
sourceEvidence.issuer: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
facts: Index lists PMAY-U 2.0 English and Hindi Scheme Guidelines dated September 2024.
Index lists Affordable Housing in Partnership Standard Operating Procedure dated April 2026.
Index also lists legacy PMAY-U amendments; applicability to PMAY-U 2.0 must be distinguished by reviewers.

sourceEvidence.title: PMAY-U 2.0 Scheme Guidelines (English)
sourceEvidence.issuer: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
facts: Beneficiary family comprises husband, wife and unmarried sons and/or unmarried daughters.
Urban EWS/LIG/MIG families must not own a pucca house in the name of the beneficiary or any family member anywhere in India, subject to guideline provisions.
Central annual household income bands: EWS up to ₹3 lakh; LIG ₹3 lakh to ₹6 lakh; MIG ₹6 lakh to ₹9 lakh. States/UTs may redefine EWS with Ministry concurrence.

Guideline states prior allotment under a government housing scheme in the preceding 20 years in urban or rural areas disqualifies the family; parent housing-benefit provision is separately framed as a prioritisation rule.
The scheme contains distinct verticals (BLC, AHP, ARH and ISS) with component-specific conditions.

sourceEvidence.title: PMAY-U 2.0 Affordable Housing in Partnership Standard Operating Procedure
sourceEvidence.issuer: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
sourceEvidence.publishedOrRevised: April 2026; 39-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted 4 November 2026
facts: The SOP covers public/private project registration, project appraisal/approval, beneficiary application, State/UT/ULB roles, monitoring, allotment and handover.

A beneficiary family includes husband, wife and unmarried sons/daughters; the application flow requires details of all family members including Aadhaar details, date of birth, relationship and occupation.
AHP EWS/LIG/MIG income bands are up to ₹3 lakh, ₹3–6 lakh and ₹6–9 lakh respectively, subject to the master guideline and State/UT EWS flexibility.

The AHP application flow includes Aadhaar OTP authentication, family details, existing-house and income details, income-certificate upload, project selection and active bank-account/IFSC details. One Aadhaar number can be used for only one form; the SOP states a married female applicant must provide husband Aadhaar details. JanaSetu must not collect Aadhaar, OTP or bank credentials.

The SOP states that mere submission does not create a right to benefits; approval/release depends on due diligence, verification and compliance. It also contains a prior-housing exclusion for AHP that must be reconciled with the master guideline’s 20-year rule; the master Scheme Guidelines prevail where there is a conflict.
The SOP describes a five-year lock-in before a beneficiary may voluntarily opt for buy-back of an allotted AHP house; this is post-allotment process, not an eligibility input.
Project-side AHP conditions include project/land appraisal and EWS project composition requirements; these must not be confused with individual household eligibility.

sourceEvidence.title: Angikaar 2026 Operational Guidelines
sourceEvidence.issuer: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
facts: The 2026 last-mile outreach campaign ran from 4 May to 31 July 2026.
The document concerns outreach, application facilitation, project completion, geo-tagging, occupancy and convergence; it is not a replacement for PMAY-U 2.0 beneficiary eligibility rules.
The PMAY-U guideline index lists the April 2026 AHP SOP and the September 2024 master guidelines; no separate current SOP for all other verticals was identified in this review.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: Urban residence and applicable urban local body jurisdiction
eligibilityMatrix.gap: No ULB, urban-area residence evidence or migration/parental-house nuances.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Define required residency proof and how rural-house ownership affects the no-pucca-house condition.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: Beneficiary family definition and no pucca house anywhere in India
eligibilityMatrix.gap: No household members, ownership shares, definition of pucca house, rural house check or exceptions.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Map each family member and ownership condition; define evidence and edge cases.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: Income band EWS/LIG/MIG and State/UT EWS flexibility
eligibilityMatrix.gap: Does not distinguish EWS/LIG/MIG, household income evidence, State/UT EWS redefinition or component-specific income criteria.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Create vertical-specific income bands and current State/UT overrides with source references.

eligibilityMatrix.condition: No housing-scheme allotment in preceding 20 years
eligibilityMatrix.gap: No scheme/date/beneficiary family member/urban-rural distinction; parent housing benefit is a separate prioritisation clause.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Separate disqualification from prioritisation and define exact 20-year calculation.

eligibilityMatrix.implementation: No vertical selection or vertical-specific rules
eligibilityMatrix.gap: The generic screen cannot establish project, land title, beneficiary contribution, loan/property limits or other component conditions.
eligibilityMatrix.reviewerAction: Do not enable deterministic assessment until vertical-specific rule packs and State/ULB workflows are reviewed.

boundaryTests.expected: Reviewer must confirm inclusive band boundaries and any State/UT override.

boundaryTests.scenario: Applicant owns no urban house but another defined family member owns a pucca house elsewhere in India
boundaryTests.expected: Do not return a potential match; family-wide ownership must be checked.

boundaryTests.scenario: Prior government housing allotment 19 years 11 months ago vs 20 years 1 day ago
boundaryTests.expected: Reviewer must define effective date and exact cutoff; no rounded-year logic.

boundaryTests.scenario: Applicant's parent received a house under an earlier scheme but applicant/family did not
boundaryTests.expected: Apply the distinct parent-benefit prioritisation clause; do not misclassify as automatic disqualification.

boundaryTests.scenario: Rural household or house in rural area
boundaryTests.expected: Route to PMAY-G or apply the exact PMAY-U rule; do not assume urban eligibility.

boundaryTests.scenario: ISS loan/property amounts or BLC land-title/beneficiary-contribution criteria are missing

amendmentsReviewed.item: April 2026 AHP SOP fully downloaded, text-extracted and reviewed; AHP operational interpretation and other vertical SOPs remain open.
Official guideline index checked 04.11.2026; legacy amendments listed but not all reconciled.

unresolvedQuestions: Review the four verticals independently and identify all applicable current SOPs, circulars and State/UT implementation orders; only the April 2026 AHP SOP was fully extracted in this pass.
Obtain written interpretation of the AHP SOP prior-housing exclusion against the master Scheme Guidelines’ 20-year rule; the master guidelines state that they prevail in case of conflict.
Confirm current State/UT EWS income modifications, urban-residency evidence, ULB verification and project-specific eligibility requirements.
Do not collect Aadhaar numbers, Aadhaar OTPs, family Aadhaar, bank account details or income documents in JanaSetu; refer applicants to the official PMAY-U portal/ULB/CSC.
Do not reduce vertical-specific AHP/ISS/BLC/ARH requirements to the prototype’s generic household fields.
